solutionSteps: \textnormal{Let }S_N\textnormal{ include the terms with indices zero through N minus one. The first omitted magnitude is }b_N\textnormal{.}
\textnormal{The magnitudes decrease to zero. The alternating-series theorem therefore bounds the error by the first omitted magnitude.}
\textnormal{Since these bounds decrease with N, every smaller positive N also fails the requested guarantee.}

solutionSteps: \textnormal{The exponential series converges uniformly on every bounded real interval, so it may be integrated term by term.}
\textnormal{The seventh power comes from index three. Its coefficient retains both the factorial and the integration factor.}
\textnormal{For any fixed nonzero x, the ratio of successive nonzero term magnitudes tends to zero. At zero convergence is immediate, so the radius is infinite.}
